title: The Encapsulation of Cell-free Transcription and Translation Machinery in Vesicles for the Construction of Cellular Mimics
protocol: Purify plasmid DNA from E. coli DH5a or Nova Blue using a commercial kit.
Elute the purified DNA with water only.
Phenol-chloroform extract the DNA solution.
Determine the DNA concentration and purity, e.g., by UV absorbance.
Weigh dry lipid powder and dissolve in chloroform at 40 mg/ml for POPC stock solutions.
Store POPC stock solutions in air-tight amber glass bottles under argon at -20°C.
Aliquot 12 μmol (220 μl) of POPC from the stock solution into a 5 ml round bottom flask.
Evaporate chloroform using a rotary evaporator to generate a thin lipid film.
Ensure that the system is open to the atmosphere by checking that the stopcock is open.
Turn on the vacuum pump and slowly close the stopcock to apply the vacuum to the system.
Let the rotary evaporation continue for 0.5-2 hr.
Slowly release the vacuum pressure, stop the rotation, and remove the round bottom flask.
Add 1 ml 18.2 MΩ H2O to the thin lipid film directly in the round bottom flask.
Vigorously vortex the solution at maximum speed until the lipid film detaches from the glass.
Transfer the lipid dispersion into a 2 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Rinse the dispersing element of the homogenizer by immersing the tip in 18.2 MΩ H2O and running for a few seconds.
Place the dispersing element directly into the lipid dispersion ensuring that the tip does not touch the bottom of the microcentrifuge tube.
Homogenize for 1 min at power level 4 or 14,000 rpm.
Assemble the parts of the mini-extruder.
Place two O-rings into the grooves of the internal membrane supports.
Prewet two filters and one 400 nm membrane.
Place the membrane between the two filters inside the Teflon.
Insert the membrane supports with filters and membrane into the extruder outer casing.
Place the Teflon bearing inside the casing.
Attach the retainer nut and tighten by hand.
Rinse two syringes and fill one with 18.2 MΩ water.
Insert the syringe needles into the small holes in the Teflon on either end of the assembly.
Pass the water through the extruder by slowly pushing it from one syringe to the other.
Repeat the passage for a total of three times, ensuring no leaks are present.
Remove and dispose of the syringe containing the water.
Fill one syringe with the sample and attach it to the extruder.
Pass the vesicle solution through the membrane as described in step 4.3, repeating this process 10 times for a total of 11 passages.
Transfer the extruded vesicle solution and make 40 μl aliquots into microcentrifuge tubes.
Flash freeze each aliquot using either dry ice or liquid nitrogen.
Lyophilize each aliquot with a centrifugal evaporator overnight at 30 °C.
Store the lyophilized empty vesicles at -20°C.
Mix the components of the transcription-translation reaction and add 20 units of RNase inhibitor.
Incubate on ice.
Add DNA template to the reaction mixture.
Bring the final volume to 25 μl with RNase-free water.
Hydrate an aliquot of lyophilized vesicles with 10 μl of the assembled transcription-translation reaction.
Vortex the mixture until vesicles are resuspended.
Incubate the reaction on ice for 30 min.
Dilute the vesicle mixture 20-fold to a final volume of 30 μl.
Add 1.5 μl of vesicles into 27.0 μl of 50 mM Tris-HCl, 50 mM NaCl, pH 7.4.
Add 1.5 μl of 20.2 mg/ml Proteinase K to the mixture.
Incubate for at least 2.5 hr at 37 °C.
Prepare a sample chamber by placing a 20 x 5 mm silicon spacer onto a standard microscope slide.
Pipette 10 μl of vesicles into the sample chamber.
Place a siliconized glass cover slip over the chamber.
Observe the vesicles with a 63X oil-dispersion or similar objective by bright field and fluorescence microscopy using the appropriate filter set for the exploited fluorescent protein.
